about: A Rust library for reading and writing Excel spreadsheet files.

prs.title: "Between" rules in spreadsheets keep both limits
prs.broken: A data check like "a whole number between 1 and 10" lost both numbers when the file was saved, so the rule no longer checked anything.
prs.changed: Both limits are now written when the file is saved.
prs.matters: Spreadsheets keep their input checks after being opened and saved.

prs.title: Charts on sheets named like O'Brien no longer crash saving
prs.broken: Saving a workbook crashed when a chart sat on a sheet whose name had an apostrophe, such as O'Brien.
prs.changed: Sheet names with apostrophes are now read and written back correctly in chart references.
prs.matters: Workbooks with everyday names like O'Brien save without crashing.

prs.title: Adding or removing rows changes only the sheet you named
prs.broken: Inserting or deleting a row or column on one sheet did the same to every other sheet in the file. Rows on other sheets were silently lost when it was saved.
prs.changed: Row and column edits now move only the cells of the sheet that was named.
prs.matters: Editing one sheet no longer quietly destroys data on the others.

prs.title: Removing rows no longer crashes on whole-column formulas
prs.broken: Deleting a row or column crashed the program if any formula used a whole column, like a sum of column A. Inserting left such formulas pointing at the wrong place.
prs.changed: Whole-column and whole-row references now move with the edit like any other reference.
prs.matters: Common spreadsheets with column totals can be edited without crashing or wrong results.
